summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of Employee Leave Hub (DRAXLMAIER, Romanian). Backend: 30/30 pytest tests passed covering auth (3 roles + bad password), /auth/me with populated department, working-days preview (incl. RO 2026 holidays), full request lifecycle (create PENDING, DRAFT→SUBMIT, cross-employee 403, insufficient balance in Romanian, manager reject-without-comment 400, cross-department approve 403, approve with atomic balance decrement, cancel PENDING vs APPROVED, PDF only for APPROVED with valid %PDF header, admin delete refunds balance, admin scope=all), attachments (CM requires attachment Romanian error, upload + retrieve base64), dashboard (USER/DEPT_RESP/ADMIN), calendar, admin CRUD (duplicate email + duplicate leave-type code Romanian errors, delete department blocked when users assigned, user CRUD cycle). Frontend: E2E happy path via Playwright — logged in as employee/maria, created CO request 2026-06-15→2026-06-16 (2 working days confirmed by preview), logged out, logged in as manager.it, viewed team requests, opened detail (workflow history visible), approved → status became 'Aprobată', PDF button appeared. Role-based sidebar verified for USER (no Team/Users/Departments), DEPT_RESP (Team present, Users hidden), ADMIN (all admin items present).

issues: Default selected leave type is CM (sorted by code alphabetically) which requires attachment — surprising UX. Consider defaulting to CO (most common) or showing an explicit placeholder until user picks.
Console warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby` for DialogContent — add DialogDescription for accessibility (non-blocking).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 835 lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, users, departments, leave_types, leave_requests, dashboard, pdf) for maintainability.

APPROVE balance deduction (line 513) uses $inc but is NOT wrapped in a transaction with the status update on line 526 — theoretical race where balance decrements but status update fails leaving the user underpaid. Low risk single-instance but should be fixed via Mongo transaction or reversed order (update status first, then $inc conditionally).
GET /api/leave-requests scope='department' with a DEPT_RESP who has no dept_id silently returns only their own request (line 371-372) — should probably 403 or empty list explicitly.
Admin creating another user with `dept_id` never validates the dept exists (oid() only checks format) — could create dangling refs.
No pagination on list_leave_requests / list_users — capped at 500/1000 with .to_list(). Fine for MVP; add pagination when volume grows.
N+1 pattern in _enrich_request (per-doc lookups for user + dept + leave_type + attachments). For large lists consider $lookup aggregation.
LoginPage prefills admin credentials in state — great for demo, but should be gated behind a NODE_ENV check for production.
test_credentials: Loaded from /app/memory/test_credentials.md (admin, 3 managers, 5 employees). All login successfully.
seed_data_creation: Test suite creates transient records (leave requests for Maria/Ion, one TEST_ user) and cleans up via admin delete/cancel. Pre-seeded ion.popescu PENDING request (2026-03-02→2026-03-06, 5 days) remains untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_leave_hub.py — run: pytest backend/tests/ -v. Uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from env. Fixture-scoped module tokens. Ordered TestLeaveRequestFlow (test_1..test_13) uses class attrs — do NOT parallelize inside class (pytest-xdist already schedules by loadscope which keeps them together). If seed is reset, remember DEPT_RESP account 'manager.it@draxlmaier.ro' is manager of IT department (Maria + Ion).
